If it were fully priced, consensus EPS would sit below the prior year's $0.78 by more than the share-count effect.

evidence.text: Bookings set-up for Q3 is constructive per primary documents. On the Q2 call (2026-07-23) management said RFPs rose substantially sequentially and year on year, expected gross bookings to ramp in H2, and called pre-backlog 'larger than backlog' and 'growing'. Q2 net awards were $795.7M (1.13x book-to-bill) against a street expectation of 0.95-1.01x. Peers that reported after Medpace confirm a firm demand backdrop: ICON Q2 gross bookings +24.1% y/y, book-to-bill 1.51 (07-29); Fortrea 1.06x, fourth quarter above 1.0 (07-29); Charles River DSA bookings +12.6% q/q (08-05). The market's bar for Q3 net book-to-bill is probably at or above ~1.1x after a +14.7% Q2 reaction.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bookings drive this stock. Q1 2026 book-to-bill of 0.88x with elevated cancellations: -22.63% (2026-04-22). Q2 2026 1.13x against 0.95-1.01x expected: +14.71% (2026-07-22). Record Q3 2025 bookings: +9.12% (2025-10-22).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. If the market doubted the H2 bookings ramp, the stock would not be at a 52-week high, +21% since the pre-Q2 price, with the skew paying upside. What is not priced is the actual Q3 cancellation level, which management itself calls 'a wild card'. So this is a small lean, not an edge.
evidence.independence: Peer documents, from different companies: ICON Q2 release https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729518057/en/ICON-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results (2026-07-29); Fortrea and Charles River via https://247wallst.com/cards/charles-river-laboratories-q2-2026-earnings-crl-01kz8ttt2xzsh2awyhsksd49wt. H1 2026 biotech VC was the strongest first half since 2022 (BioPharma Dive, https://biopharmadive.com/news/biotech-venture-capital-funding-2026-first-half/824881). All are July/August data; there is no Q3 peer print yet.

evidence.text: Revenue will fall as conversion slows, and management has said so. Q2 backlog conversion was 24.1% of opening backlog, and on the Q2 call management said '24% is kind of high relative to historical values, I would think that that is going to come down.' Backlog at 2026-06-30 was $3,014.2M, only +4.9% y/y, while revenue grew 17.2%. The 10-Q puts next-12-month conversion at $1,950-1,970M. So any 2027 color, which management said it might give 'possibly next Q', comes off a backlog that has grown much slower than revenue (the UBS backlog-coverage concern).
evidence.source_date: 2026-07-2x (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30; cover share count dated 2026-07-17)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print, which carried the first 2026 guide: -15.9%. The 2026-02-09 reaction is the closest analogue for a forward-growth read, and the baseline does not attribute it to one line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: management said it publicly and UBS has written about backlog coverage. If the market were pricing a 2027 slowdown, the stock would not sit at a 52-week high with upside-paid skew. Whether 2027 color comes on this call is uncertain.
evidence.independence: The UBS (Caliendo) backlog-coverage warning is cited in a CMC Markets/investing summary (https://www.cmcmarkets.com/en-gb/opto/medp-earnings-review-medpace-stock-soars-on-bookings-beat), but the article fetched did not contain it, so it is unverified. The allmind transcript (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2933069) is the same company's statement, so it is not independent.

evidence.text: The stock goes into the print at a 52-week high ($644.73), +4.5% over 5 and 20 days and ~+21% since the pre-Q2 $531.67. That is ~15% above the late-July sell-side average target (~$561; 11 of 14 analysts at Hold). Jefferies downgraded in July saying the valuation needs book-to-bill 'solidly above 1.0x'. A high bar after a +14.7% Q2 reaction makes a merely good bookings print vulnerable. This name has fallen 15-23% on two of its last four prints.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last 7 reactions: +14.71, -22.63, -15.90, +9.12, +54.67, -2.32, -7.52. Median absolute move 14.7%, 3 of 7 up. Large two-way moves; beats have not protected the stock when bookings disappointed.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up and level are in the price by definition. What this finding claims is only that the bar has risen. Short interest is moderate (5.8 days, ~7% float), so a squeeze is not the counterweight; the upside-paid skew (-2.96) is. That skew argues against this finding, which is why it stays small.
evidence.independence: Tape from the sealed baseline (spot, 52w-high flag, run-ups). Analyst ratings tally from MarketBeat via search: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MEDP/forecast/.

evidence.text: EPS has mechanical support. Medpace has beaten EPS consensus 8 of 8 quarters (average surprise +12.1%, per Earnings Whispers). The FY guide assumes 28.6M diluted shares and excludes buybacks after June 30. Shares outstanding fell to 27.91M at June 30 from 28.37M at Dec 31 after $294.7M of Q2 repurchases, and $527M of authorization remained. Q3 diluted shares should land below Q2's 28.55M even with no further buyback, about a 1% EPS tailwind against the $4.44-4.45 bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have not set the sign. Q1 2026 beat on EPS and fell 22.6% on bookings; the stock trades on awards.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The beat record is public, and analysts model the share count. If anything is unpriced, it is a few cents of EPS from Q3 buybacks the guide excludes. A buyback in Q3 at prices of $600+ is undisclosed until the release.
evidence.independence: Beat record from Earnings Whispers via search snippet (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/MEDP). The share counts come from the same 8-K.

evidence.text: Reimbursable pass-through costs are shrinking, which mechanically caps reported revenue. They were 44.2% of revenue in Q1 and 42.9% in Q2 ($303.1M of $707.3M), and on the Q2 call the CFO modelled '41% to 42% of revenue Q3, Q4'. Direct service revenue was about $404M in Q2 (+2.4% q/q). To reach the $709-713M revenue bar at 41.5% pass-through, direct fees need about $415-417M, roughly +3% q/q. That is achievable, but it leaves little room for a large revenue beat, while margins benefit.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print in the baseline is attributable to the pass-through line alone. Revenue misses have coincided with bookings misses (Q1 2026).
evidence.why_not_priced: Inside what the company guided, so sized near zero. The derived direct-fee arithmetic (revenue less reimbursed OOP) is not a reported metric and is not in wire copy. If the market priced it, revenue consensus would sit below ~$705M; it sits at $709-713M.
evidence.independence: CFO's 41-42% statement from the call transcript https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2933069. This shares a document with the conversion finding; it is a different line.

evidence.text: Regional biotech venture data for 2026 to date (through Q3) is weak: San Diego $1.4B raised over 113 deals through Q3 2026 (-34.1% y/y, weakest since 2022), Raleigh-Durham $184.7M (-84% y/y), per Savills Q3 2026 life-science reports. National H1 2026 was strong ($9.1B, strongest first half since 2022, BioPharma Dive). The regional series is a narrow proxy for small-biotech award flow, which is Medpace's customer base.
evidence.source_date: Q3 2026 report (date read from the search snippet's description, not verified on the page)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Funding leads awards by quarters, not weeks.
evidence.why_not_priced: Regional real-estate research is not on CRO analysts' screens. But it is a narrow proxy that contradicts a broader national series (H1 strong), so it is sized below that series.
evidence.independence: Contradicted by the broader national H1 series https://biopharmadive.com/news/biotech-venture-capital-funding-2026-first-half/824881 and the UBS June 2026 funding data (+84% y/y), both via search snippets. A proxy only.

evidence.text: A first 2027 read is likely on this call. On the Q2 call management said it would give 2027 color 'possibly next Q, but certainly in the February call'. The last forward-year guide (Feb 2026, low double-digit 2026 growth) produced -15.9%. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-02-09 (2026 guide): -15.90%. 2025-02-10 (2025 guide): -7.52%. The two forward-year guides in the baseline were both sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: Direction unknown. The option market prices the magnitude (12.7% event move). It is filed so the panel sees why [sizing note removed]; it is not a directional claim.
evidence.independence: The same transcript as the bookings and conversion findings, so not independent of them.

evidence.text: Elevance's Individual ACA business is 'tracking ahead of full-year expectations with a modestly higher margin'. evidence.text: Ericsson's Q3 (15 Oct, after Nokia last spoke on 23 Jul) printed net sales of SEK 59.5bn against an LSEG consensus of SEK 55.4bn (+7%), with organic growth of +7% and Networks sales +17% q-o-q on India and Japan. That is a direct read-through to Nokia Mobile Infrastructure (Q3 consensus ~EUR 2.8bn, +2% y-o-y; Inderes) and to the revenue line, where consensus sits only at the midpoint of Nokia's 3-7% q-o-q guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nokia's own prints (rebuilt, because the baseline's 8 'moves' are share-transfer 6-Ks, verified for 15 Oct and 8 Sep): Q2 on 23 Jul 2026 beat on comparable operating profit (EUR 434m) and fell about 5-7% on the soft Q3 guide (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/nokia-s-massive-ai-orders-overshadow-soft-guidance-bofa-sees-upside/cZZYLRvR7Uu). Q1 on 23 Apr missed revenue, raised the Network Infrastructure guide and rose about +6.5% (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/NOK/q1-2026/, approximate). This name trades on guidance and orders, not on reported-quarter revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nokia's revenue consensus (EUR 5,054m on 15 Oct, 5,058m on 19 Oct) did not move after Ericsson's beat, and NOK fell in the week after Ericsson rose 9-12%. Had the read-through been priced, the consensus would sit in the upper half of the guide and NOK would have tracked ERIC. Jefferies framed Ericsson's strength as specific to Ericsson ('lack of AI exposure'), and part of Ericsson's Networks margin was retroactive IPR revenue, which limits the transfer to Nokia.
evidence.independence: Ericsson's own release (https://www.ericsson.com/en/press-releases/2026/10/ericsson-reports-third-quarter-results-2026) and RTTNews (https://www.rttnews.com/3699316/ericsson-q3-profit-drops-sales-rise-simplifies-operating-structure-stock-gains.aspx) confirm the numbers; that is the same event, not an independent pointer to Nokia. It is a peer proxy: Nokia has not confirmed anything since 23 Jul.

evidence.text: Ciena (3 Sep, after Nokia's Q2) reported backlog of $8.5bn (+$0.8bn q-o-q), expected above $10bn by fiscal year end, said one month into FQ4 it had booked nearly as much as in all of FQ3, and guided FY27 revenue +30% or more. Inderes adds that Ciena is raising prices 10-20%. Nokia's own FY26 Optical+IP guide of 18-20% (Network Infrastructure 12-14%) looks conservative against that, which raises the odds of a Network Infrastructure guide raise or strong AI and cloud order commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Network Infrastructure guide raise at Q1 (23 Apr 2026) coincided with roughly +6.5% despite a revenue miss. At Q2 the guide was held (only technically raised) and the stock fell about 5-7%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Inderes's 19 Oct preview still carries Network Infrastructure at about +14% and Optical+IP at 19%, inside the existing guide, and FY consensus EBIT of EUR 2.40bn sits only slightly above the midpoint. Had a raise been expected, consensus would sit at or above the top of the range. The optical complex sold off 5-9% on 14-15 Oct on AI-funding fears, so the market is discounting optical demand rather than extrapolating Ciena.
evidence.independence: Inderes preview (https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/nokia-q326-preview-blikket-rettet-mod-ai-ordrer-og-vaekstforventninger-for-de-kommende-ar) notes that Nokia's optical and IP targets look cautious against peers and cites Ciena's price increases. Also https://app.sentisense.ai/stories/ciena-posts-record-q3-revenue-on-ai-demand-as-stock-fluctuates-09032026 (Ciena fell 10% on an in-line guide, a reminder that the sector sells in-line numbers).

evidence.text: Component and memory cost inflation is a margin risk to the outlook. Ericsson's Q3 release (15 Oct) says 'component costs are a headwind to gross margin next year'. TrendForce puts CPU, DRAM and SSD at 68% of a benchmark notebook BOM in Q3 2026, against 45% in Q1 2025. Nokia already guided Mobile Infrastructure gross margin down to 44-46% in Q3 from 49% in Q2. If Nokia echoes Ericsson on 2027, or softens its 'meaningful' Q4 step-up (FY consensus needs about EUR 1.2bn in Q4), the outlook line takes it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (23 Jul 2026): a held FY guide plus a soft Q3 guide took the stock down about 5-7% despite a profit beat. Q4 2025 (Jan 2026): a cautious 2026 guide made the stock slip (https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/nokia-oyj-HEL:NOKIA/news/nokia-slips-as-cautious-2026-guidance-disappoints-019e6a08-038d-7e20-9861-50fa3e020c0a/).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Ericsson said it publicly and still rose 9%, and Inderes lists component availability and price increases as a watch item. What is not priced is a quantified Nokia number. FY consensus sits slightly above the guide midpoint, so a margin caveat on Q4 or 2027 lands against a bar that assumes the hockey stick.
evidence.independence: TrendForce memory BOM data (https://www.implicator.ai/trendforce-memory-costs-laptop-prices/) is an industry proxy. The Inderes preview also cites Ciena's price increases and supply only balancing by 2028. Nokia itself flags component costs only as a generic risk factor (Q2 release).

evidence.text: The comparable operating profit bar sits above the company's own guide. Nokia guided Q3 comparable operating profit 'roughly flat' on Q2's EUR 434m (software revenue timing), while consensus is EUR 453m (Infront, 21 analysts) and EUR 462m (FactSet), so a print at guide (Inderes: 435) is a 4-6% miss against consensus even with revenue in line.

evidence.independence: Inderes preview (Infront consensus 453 vs Inderes 435; https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/nokia-q326-preview-blikket-rettet-mod-ai-ordrer-og-vaekstforventninger-for-de-kommende-ar). evidence.text: AI and cloud order intake is likely to fall q-o-q from Q2's EUR 2.8bn: Nokia itself warned the Q2 level should not be expected every quarter, and half converts within 12 months. Into a tape where the AI-funding fears of 14 Oct (SOX -4.3% that day, about -12% on the week; optical names down 5-9% on 14-15 Oct) have made AI orders the headline line, a sequential decline reads badly even if it was guided.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: record AI and cloud orders (EUR 2.8bn, sales +105% y-o-y) did not stop a 5-7% fall on the soft guide and a broad tech sell-off. Q1 2026: AI and cloud sales +49% plus a raised Network Infrastructure guide rose about +6.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company warning is public, so a modest decline is partly expected. Ciena's comment that one month of FQ4 bookings nearly matched all of FQ3 argues the other way, which is why the band is wide. If fully priced, the skew would not have calls bid.

evidence.text: Pentair, the largest pool-equipment supplier to POOL, cut channel inventory with 'major channel partners' by about $170m in Q2 (Pool segment sales -42%), guided Q3 Pool sales down 23-25%, and expects channel inventory to normalise by the end of Q3. BNP's analyst tied this to POOL, Pentair's largest customer. This implies POOL bought far less equipment in Q3, which can weigh on purchase-volume vendor incentives and gross margin. POOL's CFO said on 2026-07-23 that nothing Pentair reported changed the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has been the line: Q2 2026's 30bp margin decline plus a lower GAAP guide went -6.55%, and Q4 2025's miss went -14.48%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EBIT of $172m equals the guide's mechanics, with gross margin at -30bp. If the market priced a destock-driven hit to vendor incentives or absorption, Q3 EPS consensus would sit below the guide-implied run-rate and not on it. Pentair's Q3 numbers (due 2026-10-27) are not yet out, so the size of the Q3 destock at POOL has not been confirmed.
evidence.independence: Pentair Q3 guide of Pool -23-25% (Pentair Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000042/q22026pressrelease.htm). Barclays' Fluidra downgrade cites POOL's 'record-high inventory' and US destocking (https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/fluidra-sa-MCE:FDR/news/barclays-cuts-fluidra-to-quot-equal-weight-quot-on-us-destocking-concerns-019e6dd4-a4f0-7d70-852c-93fc9b27145d/). Counterweight: lower inventory also means stronger Q3 operating cash flow, and the CFO explicitly excluded any Pentair effect from the guide (https://www.webull.com/news/15277450926826496). This is a proxy: no POOL document quantifies it.

evidence.text: Summer 2026 (June-August) was the hottest on record for the contiguous US per NOAA: +0.4F over the prior record, a record August, record-warm summers in AZ, NM, UT and CO, and record August heat in southern Florida. Hot weather lifts chemical and maintenance volumes, POOL's largest category, in Q3. POOL's CFO called July 'pretty much on point', and Q2 sales in CA, TX and AZ were down mid-single digits.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on weather. The Q3 2025 print (sales +1%, EPS beat) went +0.91%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue growth of +1.5% is below the 2-3% H1 pace even before any weather effect, so a volume lift from record heat would show up as a revenue beat. The market has not credited it: the stock fell to a 52-week low on 10-07, a month after NOAA published.
evidence.independence: NWS Tampa summer summary (https://www.weather.gov/media/tbw/climate/summaries/Aug_Summer2026_final.pdf) shows Florida sites in the top-ten warmest. Counterweight: Leslie's reported comps -6.2% to 2026-07-04 with weather and traffic cited (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821806/000119312526346961/lesl-ex99_1.htm), and chemical price deflation continues (Q2 chemicals -2%). evidence.independence: Leslie's Q3 FY26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821806/000119312526346961/lesl-ex99_1.htm), a different document from the same company. It cuts both ways: weak consumer pool demand (negative) and an ailing competitor (positive). Any POOL receivable exposure to Leslie's is unknown.
